t: Founded by thirteen British colonies in 1776, it was the first modern republic built on a written national constitution.
It expanded across North America by purchase, war and the dispossession of Native nations; slavery ended only after civil war.
Victory in the two world wars made it a superpower, and after the fall of the Soviet Union in 1991 it was the only one.
dyk: The Constitution of the United States, in force since 1789, is the oldest written national constitution still in use.
ev: The Declaration of Independence is adopted on 4 July
The Treaty of Paris recognises American independence
The Constitution takes effect and George Washington becomes president
The Louisiana Purchase roughly doubles the country’s area
The Civil War begins after eleven Southern states secede
Union victory and the Thirteenth Amendment end slavery
The United States emerges from the Second World War as a superpower
Apollo 11 lands the first astronauts on the Moon

f.capital: Philadelphia and other seats of Congress; New York 1785–1790; Philadelphia 1790–1800; Washington, D.C. from 1800
f.founder: The Founding Fathers, among them George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, John Adams and Benjamin Franklin
f.predecessor: Thirteen British colonies of North America
